# Foundations of programing with `R`

## Functions

Functions perform actions for us. For example: 

```{r}
number_of_siblings <- c(4, 1, 7, 2, 0)
number_of_siblings
```

```{r}
sort(number_of_siblings)
```

## Packages

Most functions are stored in packages, which need to be installed and loaded before they can be used.

- installation only needs to happen once per device
```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("tidyverse")
```

- loading needs to happen once per document / R session
```{r}
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(tidyverse)
```


## Reading in data

Ex: Data from online. The input is the link to the data

```{r}
game_films <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2026/2026-06-09/game_films.csv')
```

Ex: Data from the same folder as the Quarto (.qmd) document. The input is the name of the data

```{r}
#| eval: false
unemployment <- read_csv("game_films.csv")
```

Ex: Data from an R package
```{r}
library(usdata)
data("us_crime_rates")
```


## Viewing data

Use `head()` (or `tail()`) to view the first (or last) 6 rows
```{r}
head(game_films)
tail(game_films)
```

## Viewing data

Use `glimpse()` to view column names, types, and some values
```{r}
glimpse(game_films)
```

# Creating plots

## Bar plots - Single categorical variable

```{r}
ggplot(game_films, aes(y = category)) +
  geom_bar()
```

## Histogram - Single numerical variable

```{r}
ggplot(game_films, aes(x = worldwide_box_office)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

## Using AI to improve our plot

> Prompt: Provide improvements for this plot including alt text, axis labels, and a smoothed curve. Here is my code: ggplot(game_films, aes(x = worldwide_box_office)) +
  geom_histogram()

```{r}
#| output-location: slide
ggplot(game_films, aes(x = worldwide_box_office)) +
  geom_histogram(
    aes(y = after_stat(density)),
    bins = 30,
    fill = "grey60",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_density(
    linewidth = 1,
    adjust = 1.2
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_dollar(scale = 1e-9, suffix = "B")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Worldwide Box Office Revenue",
    x = "Worldwide box office revenue (USD, billions)",
    y = "Density",
    alt = "Histogram of worldwide box office revenue for films. Most films are concentrated at the lower end of the revenue range, with a long right tail extending beyond 5 billion dollars. A smoothed density curve overlays the histogram."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

*Check that it still tells the story you wanted to deliver!*

## Scatterplot - Two numerical variables

```{r}
ggplot(game_films, aes(x = release_date, y = worldwide_box_office)) +
  geom_point()
```

## Scatterplot - Two numerical one categorical

```{r}
ggplot(game_films, aes(x = release_date, y = worldwide_box_office, color = worldwide_box_office_currency)) +
  geom_point()
```

## Scatterplot - Two numerical one categorical

```{r}
ggplot(game_films, aes(x = release_date, y = worldwide_box_office, color = worldwide_box_office_currency)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth()
```

## Computing multiple summary statistics

```{r}
game_films |> 
  filter(worldwide_box_office_currency == "$") |> 
summarize(
  median(worldwide_box_office),
  sd(worldwide_box_office)
)
  
```


## What are you expected to know?

You are expected to be able to utilize your resources to develop code to compute summary statistics, produce plots, and later on to fit models.

- I want you to decide what variable(s) you want to plot, and what the purpose of your plot / summary statistic is. 

- You can use AI to suggest pros and cons of plot types or summary statistics and to improve your plots
  - Think of AI as your simple-minded assistant that needs revision and clear guidance

# Installations

1. [Install `R`](https://www.r-project.org/)

2. [Install `RStudio`](https://docs.posit.co/ide/user/#rstudio-ide-oss-downloads)

3. The PDF (Latex) option requires an additional installation. Open RStudio and in the Console enter:

```{r}
#| eval: false
install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()
```
